newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday February 13
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday February 13

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi expressed renewed optimism that Italy would trim its 1997 budget deficit by enough to join EMU.

* The ruling coalition seems to be reconsidering the possibility of bringing forward the 1998 budget, as Prodi said there is no hurry to reform Italy's welfare system. Growing opposition to further public expenditure cuts is mounting within the former communist Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) (all).
* Italy's three main trade unions CGIL, CISL and UIL called a national demonstration in Rome on March 22 to protest against the government delaying investments to support its labour policy (all).

* Railway trade unions called off a planned strike after they reached an agreement with Transport minister Claudio Burlando on a proposed reform of state-run railway company Ferrovie dello Stato. The company will no longer be split in two by the end of 1997, one managing the rail lines and the infrastructure and the second the train and rolling stock.

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the government wants "a stable group, a hard core of shareholders" when it privatises telecoms group Stet and that it would be sufficient for such a group to hold around 10 percent of Stet stocks. He added the government's stake in the merged Stet-Telecom Italia grouping will fall below 50 percent.

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio sounded a warning on the country's cracking pensions system: "I do not want to enter the political debate, but the figures are speaking for themeselves," he said (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
